title: Order VII rule 11 CPC — Rejection of plaint

content.overview: Order VII rule 11 CPC is the rejection-of-plaint power. The court looks at the plaint and the documents referred to in it. It does not try disputed facts as if on evidence.
content.study: The usual grounds in practice are no cause of action and suit barred by law on the face of the plaint. Valuation and court-fee defaults are also enacted grounds. Rejection is not a decree after trial. If the plaint discloses a cause of action, the defendant must plead and prove the defence. Do not use rule 11 as a mini-trial of disputed title.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Quote the clause. Point to the paragraph of the plaint. If you need evidence, you are probably outside rule 11.
